1.q: The Head of Wealth asks for last quarter's AUM, then has four follow-up questions. What does a three-day turnaround actually cost her?
options: The dashboard behind the slide drifts out of date during the wait
The follow-up questions never get asked, so the insight is never reached
The first number arrives wrong and has to be corrected afterwards
The analyst spends three days assembling work of comparatively little value
1.why: Each question exists only because the previous one was answered. Latency does not slow that chain down, it ends it, and the useful insight usually sits around question four.

1.q: Which sentence tells you someone needs a Genie Agent built, rather than Genie One?
options: Show me last quarter's dashboard
I want Genie to understand my business
I have a question about my data
Help me build with data
1.why: Genie One is the front door for asking. A Genie Agent is a build activity: someone curates a governed domain first, so the answers can be trusted. Genie Code is for writing and debugging.

1.q: A data engineer needs help working out why a query returns duplicate portfolios. Which experience?
options: A Genie Agent
A saved dashboard
Genie Code
Genie One
1.why: Genie Code sits in the workspace alongside the work, writing, debugging and explaining SQL and Spark. It is also where you tune an agent later in this course.

1.q: Asking for Wealth AUM at the end of Q2 sounds like one question. Why is it really six?
options: The query needs six separate table joins before it can be resolved properly
Quarter-end figures arrive in six different source feeds
Six of its words each carry more than one defensible reading
AUM has to be recalculated separately for each asset class
1.why: Wealth, AUM, at the end of, Q2, which portfolios and which source can each be read more than one way. Answer them differently and you get six defensible numbers, only one of which is the one meant.

1.q: What does the new-analyst analogy tell you about building a Genie Agent?
options: An agent needs several weeks of live use before it becomes accurate
The agent learns your business on its own by reading query history
The agent should be given access to as many tables as you are able to grant
The work is onboarding: definitions, sources, calculations and exceptions
1.why: You would not hand a new analyst four thousand tables and ask her to work out AUM. Everything you would teach a person is what the agent needs, and what you forget to mention is where it goes wrong.

1.q: Which question separates a demo from a production-quality Genie Agent?
options: Can Genie produce a plausible answer on the very first attempt without help
How many tables can the agent read before it starts slowing
Can it answer consistently, from trusted data, and can I prove it
How quickly does the first response come back to the person
1.why: Demos are easy and nearly always succeed first time. Consistency, agreed definitions and provable accuracy are the bar, and reaching it takes curation.

1.q: Of the four ingredients (AI, Data, Business Context, Governance), which is described as the actual work, and the one most often skipped?
options: AI
Governance
Business Context
Data
1.why: The AI comes with the platform and is not your differentiator. Data is necessary but nowhere near sufficient. Business context, meaning definitions, synonyms, rules and worked examples, is what teams skip before wondering why answers drift.

2.q: Which question will Genie struggle with most?
options: What were net flows by channel for FY2026 Q3?
Why did net flows fall last quarter?
Which ten funds had the largest outflows in FY2026 Q3?
What was AUM by asset class as of 30 June 2026?
2.why: Genie can fetch numbers and do the maths. It cannot tell you why something happened. Ask for the trend and the breakdown, then form your own view of the cause.

2.q: A good question names four things. Which set is it?
options: A table, a column, a join, and a date range
A question, a chart, a filter, and a dashboard to publish it on
A measure, a cut, a filter, and a point in time
A metric, an owner, a definition, and a source
2.why: Nearly every question that fails is missing one of those four. The point in time causes the most trouble, because a balance and a period need different kinds of date.

2.q: Why is 'What was our AUM in June?' a risky way to ask?
options: June is ambiguous because the financial year starts in October each year
The word AUM is a synonym that the agent has not been taught to recognise
AUM is only published quarterly, so a monthly figure will not exist yet
AUM is a balance, so a whole month invites Genie to add up every day in it
2.why: A balance is a value at one moment. Ask for a month and Genie may total thirty daily values and return a number thirty times too big, with no error shown. Ask 'as of 30 June' instead.

2.q: You ask a question, then follow up with 'only for the Northeast'. When does that context apply?
options: Only within the same thread of conversation
Across every chat you open with that agent
Only if you restate the original question
For the rest of your session, in any agent
2.why: A thread remembers what came before. A new chat starts from nothing, which is why four separate chats give you four answers that do not add up.

2.q: You asked for discretionary portfolios only. What should you check in Show code?
options: That the query runs in under ninety seconds overall
That the query uses a join rather than a subquery
That the query returns fewer than one thousand rows in total
That something about discretion appears in the query
2.why: A dropped filter is the most common quiet failure. If nothing about discretion appears, you were given the whole book and the number will look perfectly reasonable.

2.q: What does clicking 'Fix it' on a wrong answer actually do?
options: It flags the answer for whoever maintains the agent
It reports a bug to Databricks support on your behalf
It rewrites the query and immediately runs the whole question again for you
It deletes the conversation so nobody else can reuse it
2.why: Feedback is how the agent's owner finds problems. Rating a good answer can also prompt Genie to offer them a reusable snippet, so the two seconds are worth spending.

3.q: Which mode can answer questions about PDFs in a Unity Catalog volume?
options: Neither
Agent mode
Chat mode
Both equally
3.why: Chat mode requires structured data. Agent mode can analyse unstructured files the author attached to the agent.

3.q: How many SQL queries does Chat mode typically run per question?
options: One
One per table in the agent
As many as needed
Three to five
3.why: Chat mode generates a single query. Agent mode builds a research plan and runs many queries, iterating on what it finds.

3.q: What is the availability caveat for Agent mode?
options: Requires a separate paid Genie Code licence for every person in the workspace
Limited to workspaces that hold fewer than thirty agents in one metastore
Available in Americas and Europe workspaces; elsewhere needs cross-Geo processing enabled
Available only on serverless warehouses running in a single cloud region, with no exceptions
3.why: Teach it as 'check your workspace' rather than a fixed answer, since regional availability changes.

4.q: In the influence hierarchy, which input has the strongest effect on an answer?
options: A trusted asset (verified query or UC function)
Chat history
A plain-text instruction written in the Instructions panel
A Unity Catalog table comment
4.why: Trusted assets say 'use this exact logic'. Plain-text instructions rank weakest, they are the last resort, not the first tool.

options: Only if they include ground-truth SQL
No: they only measure accuracy
Yes, but only in Agent mode
Yes, they act as extra examples
4.why: Instructions and examples change answers. Benchmarks grade them. Learners confuse these constantly.

4.q: Which layer is the only real guarantee of Genie's behaviour?
options: Unity Catalog: row filters, column masks and grants
The benchmark set, once it covers every question asked
Trusted assets, because their SQL has been verified
The knowledge store, once its synonyms and joins are complete
4.why: Genie has built-in randomness. Everything above Unity Catalog is guidance that makes the right answer more likely, not a guarantee.

4.q: A stakeholder says 'I got a different number yesterday.' What is the most likely explanation?
options: The underlying data was reloaded overnight by the pipeline
A different thread, a different mode, or a genuinely ambiguous definition
Genie's underlying model was upgraded since they last asked
Their Unity Catalog permissions were changed between the two runs
4.why: Earlier turns are context, Chat and Agent scores are not comparable, and an unresolved definition legitimately produces more than one defensible answer.

5.q: At Meridian, how many defensible readings does 'return' have for a single portfolio and period?
options: One, defined by the performance team and published
Three: gross of fees, net of fees, and money weighted
Two, being the portfolio return and the benchmark return
Four, because each of the six period types counts once
5.why: twr_gross, twr_net and mwr all sit in fct_performance, and all three are honest answers to 'what was our return?'. The table also holds benchmark_return, which is not the portfolio's return at all.

5.q: What does the glossary template require for every term?
options: A named owner and an implementation route
Sign-off from the CFO before it can be used
A SQL definition and nothing else besides
A benchmark question proving the definition
5.why: Without a named owner the definition never gets decided; without an implementation route it never reaches the agent.

5.q: Which statement best captures this module's teaching line?
options: Metric views solve definition problems automatically
Genie needs more example queries
Business users ask badly formed questions
Genie didn't get it wrong: your company has three answers and never picked one
5.why: Most 'AI accuracy problems' are unresolved definition problems wearing a technical costume.

6.q: Which credential type determines what data a user can see?
options: The warehouse owner's identity
Data credentials: the asking user's own identity
The agent's service principal
Compute credentials embedded by the author
6.why: Compute credentials decide which warehouse runs the query; data credentials are the user's identity, so row filters and column masks apply per user.

6.q: What is the correct way to stop PII appearing in Genie answers?
options: Hiding the columns in the agent
A text instruction saying 'never show PII'
Restricting the agent to CAN VIEW
Column masks in Unity Catalog
6.why: An instruction is guidance, not a control, demonstrate it failing. Masks and row filters are the only enforcement.

6.q: 340 regional sales leads need to ask questions and give feedback but must not change business logic. Which level?
options: CAN MANAGE
CAN VIEW
CAN RUN
CAN EDIT
6.why: CAN EDIT would let any of them change definitions for everyone. CAN VIEW would not let them ask questions at all.

6.q: Priya (Northeast) and Marcus (West) ask the identical AUM question and get different totals. What happened?
options: The agent has a join error that duplicates advisor rows for one region
The agent is nondeterministic and varies between runs
One of them ran the question in Agent mode instead
Unity Catalog row filters were correctly enforced per user
6.why: Same agent, same question, three correct answers. Genie leaked nothing, this is the governance model working.

7.q: What is the maximum number of tables or views in one Genie Agent, and the recommended starting size?
options: 30 maximum, start with 5 or fewer
No hard maximum, start small
30 maximum, start with 20
50 maximum, start with 10
7.why: Beyond 30 you cannot add more; beyond about 5 the agent gets measurably worse at routing and slower to think.

7.q: Why replace the 380-column fct_holdings_raw with a slim view?
options: Every column is context Genie must read, so width costs both accuracy and speed
It reduces the storage cost of the warehouse considerably
Column masks can only be applied to views rather than to the underlying base table
Genie does not support tables wider than about two hundred columns
7.why: Narrow is faster, not just more accurate. Module 13 puts a stopwatch on exactly this.

7.q: When should you build a metric view instead of curating the metric inside the agent?
options: Always, because an agent should never contain metric logic of its own under any circumstances
When the metric must mean the same thing across several agents, dashboards and reports
Only once the agent exceeds the thirty-object limit
Only for metrics that are used inside Agent mode research
7.why: Five agents each defining 'net flows' slightly differently is a finding in asset management, not merely a trust problem, particularly when one of them feeds a client report. Metric views exist to prevent it.

7.q: Genie Code suggests a description for fee_revenue. What should you do?
options: Bulk-accept all suggestions, then fix failures later
Accept it: it read the data
Verify it against the business definition before accepting
Reject all AI suggestions on principle
7.why: The docs call out unverified AI-generated descriptions specifically. In this dataset the suggestions get the gross-vs-net flaw wrong on purpose.

8.q: Why should you never bulk-accept the Genie Code bootstrap suggestions?
options: Each one consumes budget and, if wrong, teaches the agent something false
They cannot be edited once they have been accepted
They count against the benchmark question limit
They silently overwrite the Unity Catalog comments that already exist underneath
8.why: Suggestions draw down your 100 instructions and 200 snippets, and a confidently wrong description is worse than no description.

8.q: A 'common question' starter chip returns a wrong answer. How should this be treated?
options: As low priority, since starters are just examples
As a benchmark failure only
As expected variation
As a P1 bug: it is the first thing every new user clicks
8.why: The starter chips are the entire onboarding experience for a business user. They must be questions the agent answers perfectly today.

8.q: Which agent description is more useful to a business user in Genie One?
options: 'Wealth & Distribution v2 (final). Supersedes v1. Reads mfg_core_fct_aum_snapshot, mfg_core_fct_flows, mfg_core_fct_performance and nine dimension tables.'
'Wealth agent. Built by the analytics team on the genie_agent schema and refreshed nightly. Contact the data team with any questions about coverage or availability.'
'Wealth & Distribution: AUM, net flows and performance by portfolio, fund, channel and region. AUM means discretionary market value. Fiscal year starts 1 October. Owner: Wealth Analytics.'
'Agent for the Wealth business. Ask it anything about assets, flows, clients, advisors, funds, portfolios, performance, benchmarks, regions and channels.'
8.why: The description is how users decide which agent to open. Name the audience, the metrics, the owner and the calendar, and define the contested word before anyone has to ask.

9.q: What is the knowledge-store snippet limit per agent?
options: About 200
9.why: Descriptions, join relationships and SQL expressions all draw on the same ~200 budget. Past it, extra context stops being used.

options: 200 columns, 200 values each
Unlimited columns, 100 values each
30 columns, 500 values each
120 columns, 1,024 values each
9.why: Enable it for every low-cardinality categorical column users name out loud, region, state, status, channel, category.

9.q: Genie reports total AUM as $67.2 trillion instead of $98.5 billion. What is the root cause?
options: It summed a daily snapshot across every date rather than filtering to one
A currency conversion joined the wrong as-of date for the reporting period
The warehouse was too small to complete the aggregation correctly
It reported assets under advisement rather than assets under management
9.why: Measured on the real dataset, summing the snapshot overstates the book by 682x. This is the scariest failure in the course because nothing errors. Fix it in the data layer, the join specification and the column description.

9.q: 'Posted transactions only' (status = 'POSTED') should be implemented as which kind of SQL expression?
options: A measure
A filter
A field
A text instruction
9.why: Filters capture reusable conditions, measures capture KPIs, fields capture derived attributes. Encoding this as prose is the classic mistake.

10.q: How does the 100-instruction budget count items?
options: Only text blocks count
Example queries count as one; functions are free
Every example query, every function and every text block counts as one
It counts total characters, not items
10.why: It is separate from the 200 knowledge-store snippets. Leaving headroom for what monitoring reveals is professional practice.

10.q: What happens when a text instruction block grows past roughly 5,000–7,000 characters?
options: It is automatically summarised
A warning appears and Genie may silently ignore parts of it
The save is rejected
It is truncated with a visible marker
10.why: Prose does not just rank lowest in the influence hierarchy, past a certain length it can be dropped without telling you.

10.q: How should you title an example SQL query?
options: With a short technical identifier like q_netrev_region_fq
With the metric name only
With the user's own phrasing of the question
With the tables it touches
10.why: The title drives prompt matching. 'What was AUM by asset class as of the last reporting date?' beats any code-style name, because it is phrased the way a user would ask.

10.q: Which four parts must a clarification instruction contain?
options: Owner, definition, synonym, and grain
Trigger, missing detail, action, and an example question
Question, SQL, parameter, and comment
Metric, dimension, filter, and format
10.why: 'Ask clarification questions about AUM' is the vague version the docs call out. The template forces specificity: when to trigger, what is missing, what to do, and an example.

11.q: How many benchmark questions can one agent hold?
options: Up to 1,000
Up to 100
Up to 500
Up to 200
11.why: They measure accuracy only and never feed back as context.

11.q: How does benchmark scoring differ between Chat mode and Agent mode?
options: Both modes use LLM judges to score the answer that came back
Both modes compare result sets against the ground truth
Chat compares result sets to ground-truth SQL; Agent uses LLM judges
Agent mode cannot be benchmarked at all, so it must be reviewed by hand
11.why: Because the two scores are produced differently, they are not comparable, never average them.

11.q: You correct Genie's bad SQL in a response. What is the highest-value next step?
options: Save it as an example query, then add it to the benchmark set
Delete the conversation
Email the corrected number to the requester
Add a text instruction describing the fix
11.why: Every 'Fix it' is a free curation task with the answer already attached, that is what makes the fix permanent.

11.q: Why is a single before/after comparison insufficient evidence that a change helped?
options: Chat mode caches previous answers, so the second run is not fresh
Genie varies by design, so one comparison cannot separate improvement from noise
The Monitor tab reports quality on a weekly cycle only
Benchmarks are only considered valid once they contain at least five hundred questions
11.why: Run a set, same mode, fresh chat, same agent version. Two side-by-side questions is an anecdote, not a measurement.

12.q: Users ask about 'California' and get zero rows. What is the right fix?
options: Rename the column to state_code
Add a text instruction listing state codes
Entity matching on the state column
Tell users to type 'CA'
12.why: Fabricated filter values are among the most common causes of wrong answers. Curate the real values so Genie matches phrasing to data.

12.q: Genie states that 'outflows rose because of the fee change'. How should an author treat this?
options: As expected Agent mode behaviour that needs no action
As a valid insight worth forwarding to the CIO
As an unsupported causal claim to be diagnosed and tightened
As a benchmark failure to be recorded and scored
12.why: Genie retrieves, it does not diagnose. Tighten the context, remove overlapping tables, and inspect the reasoning with Genie Code.

12.q: Routing quality is degrading across the whole workspace. What often helps?
options: Deleting old and unused agents
Adding more example queries to each agent
Raising the instruction limit
Increasing the warehouse size
12.why: Too many agents hurts routing for everyone. Portfolio hygiene is an operational task, not a one-off.

13.q: In a typical slow Genie response, where does most of the time go?
options: Fetching results from the warehouse
Thinking: routing, reading context and writing SQL (~20s+)
Query execution (~20s+)
Rendering the visualisation
13.why: Query execution is usually only 3–10 seconds. This is why doubling the warehouse so often changes nothing.

13.q: What is the SQL query time limit, and can it be raised?
options: 90 seconds, and it cannot be raised
300 seconds, raisable by support
90 seconds, raisable on serverless
597 seconds, and it cannot be raised
13.why: Keep the warehouse warm and filter or cluster large tables instead. Treating it as a config knob wastes time.

13.q: What happens at the ~597 second backend ceiling?
options: The query is retried automatically
A runaway answer that is billed but never shown
The user sees a clear timeout message
The conversation is deleted
13.why: Set client and orchestrator timeouts below it, or you pay for answers nobody ever sees.

13.q: A naive polling loop in your own integration was measured adding how much delay?
options: It adds none
Under 1 second
About 30 seconds
About 6–8 seconds
13.why: Instrument your poll loop as its own span. That latency is yours, not Genie's, and it gets blamed on Genie.

13.q: query.history shows a high waiting_at_capacity_duration_ms. What does that point to?
options: A slow federated join reaching an external system
Too much context for the model to read through before it can begin planning the query
A cold start on a warehouse that had gone to sleep
Warehouse queueing or overload: scale up, use auto mode, or dedicate a warehouse
13.why: High waiting_for_compute points to cold start; a big gap before EXECUTING_QUERY with small SQL means thinking dominates.

14.q: Which piece of evidence matters most when filing a Genie issue?
options: The number of tables in the agent
The message ID: captured before starting a fresh chat
A screenshot of the answer and the chart beneath it
The warehouse size
14.why: Without it, support cannot trace the request. Learners lose it constantly by refreshing first.

14.q: You see '429 / rate limit exceeded'. What is happening?
options: The conversation limit was reached
You are hitting shared AI model capacity (200 requests/sec)
The warehouse is out of slots
Your budget threshold blocked you
14.why: Reduce the request rate and move heavy or automated use to dedicated capacity. Sequential fan-out from an integration is the usual cause.

14.q: The SQL ran correctly but the response says 'AI service did not respond with a valid answer'. What is this?
options: A curation problem, so the fix is to add more worked examples to the agent
Expected variation between runs of the same question
A permissions error on one of the underlying tables
A platform bug in the answer-assembly step: file it with the message ID
14.why: No amount of curation fixes it. Recognising this saves days of pointless tuning.

14.q: A customer demands guaranteed identical answers every time. Where does that requirement land?
options: On Unity Catalog: row and column security
On Agent mode, which is deterministic
On the benchmark set, once it covers every question
On the knowledge store and its synonyms
14.why: Everything above Unity Catalog is guidance, not a guarantee. Say so before the customer discovers it.

15.q: How much free monthly LLM allowance does a service principal get?
options: None: all its usage is charged
Half a user's allowance
The same as a user
It cannot be billed
15.why: Critical for integrations: an API client running as a service principal is billed from message one.

15.q: Which resource type and tag are used to set a Genie budget?
options: Unity Catalog, tagged billing: genie
Model Serving, tagged genie: true
Unity AI Gateway, tagged databricks-product: genie
SQL Warehouse, tagged product: genie
15.why: Budgets are set by account admins in the account console. The free per-user allowance cannot be removed by a budget.

15.q: What is the recommended blocking policy?
options: Block service principals; alert on humans
Block humans; alert on service principals
Never enable blocking
Block everyone at the shared threshold
15.why: A runaway integration loop is the real cost risk. Blocking a regional sales lead during a quarter-end client review is not.

16.q: What is the default architectural choice, a Supervisor Agent or calling Genie directly?
options: Use a supervisor whenever there is more than one agent
Call Genie directly; add a supervisor only for what Genie structurally lacks
Use a supervisor to improve answer quality
Always use a supervisor for production
16.why: Every layer multiplies thinking time and rate-limit exposure. A supervisor adds capability, never speed.

16.q: Where should a supervisor's orchestrator timeout be set?
options: At 90 seconds to match the SQL limit
As high as possible to avoid dropped answers
Exactly at 597 seconds
Below the ~597 second backend ceiling
16.why: Past the ceiling you are billed for answers that never return.

16.q: In serialized_space, what format must every ID use?
options: 32-character lowercase hexadecimal
Any unique string
Sequential integers
UUID v4 with dashes
16.why: Collections must also be alphabetically sorted, and join_specs.sql needs exactly two elements, the condition and a relationship-type annotation.

16.q: What do you lose by collapsing an integration to a single service principal?
options: Only the free LLM allowance
Only Agent mode support
Nothing: it is the recommended pattern
Per-user row filters and column masks, plus the free LLM allowance
16.why: In a bank that is a control failure, not an optimisation. Preserve user identity.

17.q: Which two rubric criteria carry the most points?
options: Knowledge store depth and measured accuracy (18 each)
Scope & purpose and business communication
Instructions quality and data preparation
Governance and performance
17.why: Depth of semantics and honest measurement are what separate a demo from something a business will trust.

17.q: Beyond 70 points, what else must a capstone do to pass?
options: Cover all thirty permitted tables in a single agent
Tier-1 smoke tests at 100%, and state the agent's limits and that consistency is guidance
Include a Supervisor Agent routing across at least three separate business domains and tools
Use Agent mode for every question in the benchmark set
17.why: Stating limits is a graded requirement, it is what makes an agent trustworthy in production.

17.q: The capstone requires a performance baseline. What must it show?
options: A benchmark score above ninety percent overall
The warehouse size, the monthly cost it implies, and the budget thresholds set
A measured thinking-vs-query split, one applied fix, and its measured effect
Query time held under ninety seconds throughout
17.why: Diagnosis before tuning is the graded skill, exactly as in Module 13's lab.
